input: Look into long-term care insurance for my parents

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of parents (one or two), their ages, and current health status heavily influence eligibility, premiums, and whether joint or individual policies make sense.
Knowing whether this is early-stage awareness research, active plan comparison, or helping parents enroll determines how deep and actionable the plan needs to be.
The state or country where parents live affects which insurers operate there, regulatory protections, and Medicaid interaction rules.
A monthly premium budget sets hard limits on which plans are realistic and whether hybrid or traditional LTC policies are feasible.
Whether the user wants to do this research themselves, involve a financial advisor, or loop in their parents directly changes the recommended next steps.
Priorities like in-home care vs. facility care, benefit duration, or inflation protection shape which policy features to focus on.
Understanding what a successful outcome looks like — a shortlist of providers, a comparison spreadsheet, a policy purchased — defines the finish line for this task.

gold.taskTitle: Research long-term care insurance for parents
gold.taskDescription: Investigate long-term care insurance options suitable for the user's parents, covering what to look for, how to compare plans, and how to move forward.

questions.title: How many parents, and how old are they?
questions.description: Age and whether one or both parents are involved directly affects eligibility windows, premium costs, and whether a shared-care or joint policy is worth exploring.

questions.title: Are you researching options or ready to compare real quotes?
questions.description: This distinguishes early awareness research from active shopping, which determines how detailed and action-oriented the plan should be.

questions.title: What state or country do your parents live in?
questions.description: Location determines which insurers are licensed there, state-specific consumer protections, and how Medicaid partnership programs interact with LTC policies.

questions.title: Is there a monthly premium budget you are working within?
questions.description: A budget ceiling rules in or out certain policy types (traditional LTC, hybrid life/LTC, annuity-based) and benefit levels.

questions.title: Will you research this yourself or involve a financial advisor?
questions.description: Knowing who will do the legwork shapes whether the plan should include steps to find a specialist broker or focus on self-guided comparison tools.

questions.title: Is in-home care or facility-based care the bigger priority?
questions.description: This preference drives which policy features matter most — home care riders, facility daily benefit limits, and care coordinator services.

questions.title: What does a completed outcome look like to you?
questions.description: Clarifying the finish line — a shortlist of providers, a recommendation to parents, or a policy signed — sets the scope boundary and measures success.
